entries.not_relevant_because: The manuscript 'The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture' (Sept 23 2026) proves only that every finite set of n ≥ 2 distinct points in R^d (d ≥ 3) has at least c_d n^(2/d) distinct distances, a cardinality bound on the distance set of a finite set. Falconer's question concerns the Lebesgue measure of the distance set of an infinite set of Hausdorff dimension above d/2, and nothing in the paper passes from the finite-set count to that measure; a search of all its TeX sources finds no mention of Falconer, Hausdorff dimension, Lebesgue measure of a distance set, or infinite sets, so any link between the two problems is only the heuristic analogy the matching pass noted.
